doc.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024

title: The call to join Thelonious Monk and his wife's role
summary: Smith tells how his wife, daughter of a boxer, told him he must take the call to play with Monk, and credits her for everything he did.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah I was just imagining, you know my wife and I we have a little routine sort of when I get home from a gig she might say, “How’d it go?” Or the next morning if there was something of significance I might say, “Guess what happened last night.” So I’m envisioning the morning after that gig with Thelonious Monk where this guy comes up to you and makes this request.

Oh well that, it was months after the gig with Thelonious. It was months later. And I was coming home from a pretty stupid gig, which you know you work a number of them in the tuxedo at a country club with an accordion player, you know, like you’re feeding your family. And so I come home, it’s about 8:00 and my wife is standing at the door and she’s — my wife’s father and my wife passed away three years ago. My wife’s father © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

was a pugilist. He was a prizefighter and he was in the same stables as Jack Dempsey so he was really good. And his wife said, he says, “It’s either me or boxing. You have to give up boxing if you want me.” His wife. And so he gave up boxing. But he taught his daughter how to box. My wife. And she would, when she would get angry she would assume a pugilistic stance. You know? She just would get into that stance as if she was going to hit me. And she was standing at the door and she says, “You just got the call to go with Thelonious and you better say yes.”
I mean everything that I ever did is because of her. I mean she was the most wonderful partner for me, for a jazz musician. And she loved the music.
